articles.title: Amid surging demand, HMT plans new Bengaluru unit; targets monthly production of 25,000 watches
articles.summary: Bengaluru: HMT Ltd, India’s iconic ‘timekeeper’, plans to ramp up production to 25,000 watches a month by March and set up another manufacturing plant in Bengaluru’s Jalahalli amid a surging demand for its timepieces. The growing popularity of its watches, particularly the recently launched ‘Kannadiga’ edition, has put pressure on its existing manufacturing capacity. The company has already scaled up monthly production to 12,000 to 13,000 watches. The building is ready and the company is awaiting the necessary approvals to begin operations, HMT Ltd’s managing director N Ramesh Kumar told DH . The potential demand is so high, Kumar went on, that the company will have to ramp up production to one lakh watches a month, even by a conservative estimate. “Even if I cater to just half or one per cent of the population, the demand would be much higher than one lakh watches. This is based on public requirements, demand and media response,” he said. HMT is selling its watches through its own e-commerce portal and Amazon to cater to customers across the country and abroad. However, Karnataka, particularly Bengaluru, continues to account for the largest share of sales, with a substantial number of customers purchasing watches from HMT’s showrooms. HMT to launch four new Kannadiga watch series for Kannada Rajyotsava, prices start at Rs 3,500 Explaining the popularity of the Kannadiga edition, Kumar attributed it primarily to the emotional connect people have with the brand and the regional identity associated with the watch. “HMT has been in the hearts of people for ages,” he remarked. He added that the company was working on three new watch designs based on customer feedback but declined to reveal details until their official launch. HMT is also exploring the possibility of bringing back its classic mechanical watches, following growing demand from customers. Kumar said the company had received several requests for mechanical watches and was discussing reviving the segment. He said HMT’s emphasis on affordability and durability remained central to its approach, particularly as younger consumers, including Gen Z, were showing renewed interest in the brand. Despite the revival in demand, the company’s biggest challenge remains working capital, Kumar said. He explained that financial constraints had limited the company’s ability to scale up manufacturing and release larger quantities of watches to meet customer demand. “Working capital is a big issue for us. If we had the required funds, we could have done things multifold in no time. We are somehow managing and trying to meet people’s expectations,” Kumar said. Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H D Kumaraswamy , under whom HMT falls, said there was “tremendous demand” for HMT watches from all age groups. “On August 15 alone, transactions worth over Rs 35 lakh were recorded. People queued up for kilometres to purchase them. And on November 1, I personally launched the attractive and high-quality HMT Kannadiga collection of wristwatches. This collection, too, is witnessing overwhelming demand,” he said in a statement to DH . Kumaraswamy said he had made significant efforts to revive the HMT watch division, which was technically shut down, and efforts were also underway to revive the entire HMT factory. Mohan, a watch enthusiast, said buying HMT watches brings back memories of “watching our fathers and grandfathers wear those timepieces”.
